names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 10 iunie, «Sfânta Muceniță Antonina».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 10 Ιουνίου, «Άγιοι Αλέξανδρος και Αντωνίνα», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 10. јун ст. ст., „Свети мученик Александар и Антонина“, which names the two of them. Свети is not a rank and мученик is the `martyr` this corpus puts in `types` — and the heading uses it in the singular for a pair, which is the book’s own looseness and not a reading — so both come off and the bare personal name is the whole of the form. THE FOLD IS DELIBERATE: `foldchk.py` returns `[('antonina-of-nicaea', 'sr')]`, so this makes a fold of two; the heading gives the bare forename and the city is in the body, which §6 does not let into a form.

The name as name page 2400 gives it, «Мученица Антонина Кродамнская», with the grade taken off; the epithet is the Crodamna this folder's English name already carries. Measured with the gate's own fold before it was written: 'антонина кродамнская' has no other holder, where the folder's existing Serbian form is the bare «Антонина».

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 10 июня ст. ст. — «Мчч. Александра и Антонины девы (ок. 313).»

attestations.note: The day's seventh entry names the two together, «Мчч. Александра и Антонины девы (ок. 313).», and the Romanian, Greek and Serbian rows of both folders already stand on this same 10 June, so the day and the identity were not in doubt. The line's «ок. 313» is this folder's own 313 and nothing in `dates` was touched. Each of the two has a name page of its own — 105 «Мученик Александр Воин» and 2400 «Мученица Антонина Кродамнская» — each giving «День памяти: 10 июня» and no other day, and each listing the same two readings of the pair under «Жития». Those readings were NOT opened: both folders already carry a life and three hymns apiece from the other calendars, and this upgrade adds the Russian day and the Russian name form only. The day page prints no hymn for either. azbyka.ru was not read.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 10 iunie — «Sfânta Muceniță Antonina»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 10ης Ιουνίου — «Άγιοι Αλέξανδρος και Αντωνίνα»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 10 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and dates both «(; - 313)». It is plainly the same woman: the Christian virgin of «της κωμόπολης Καρδάμου (ή Kροδάμου)» — the page gives both forms of her town's name, and Krodamos is the folder's own — denounced to the eparch Phystus, thrown into a brothel, delivered by an earthquake at her prayer, got out by Alexander in his clothes, and burnt with him. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 23.06.2026 (10. јун ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Александар и Антонина“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, whose heading names them both. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. A FIRST DATE, AND IT IS A YEAR TWO BOOKS HAD CITED AND NEITHER HAD RECORDED. Both folders held `dates: null`. `antonina-of-crodamna`’s own life says doxologia «gives no year» and then quotes saint.gr’s head line, «(; - 313)», **without that year ever reaching `dates`** — which is `date-citation-audit.mjs`’s shape exactly, a year cited and never written down. This book states it flat and adds a day: „Чесно пострадаше ради љубави Христове и преселише се у дворе Цара небескога 3. маја 313. године“. Two books, one flat year, no approximation: `death` 313 to 313, `basis` `traditional`. **THE 3 MAY IS NOT WRITTEN AS A FEAST AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.** The book gives it as the date they passed, not as a day it keeps them on — it keeps them on the Julian 10 June, which is the heading this row quotes and the menologion number the Romanian and Greek rows carry. **No second day, no §4 note, nothing moved**; the 3 May is in the life as the book’s own statement and in this note, and a later reader who meets a 3 May commemoration elsewhere should read this before deciding anything. ONE DIFFERENCE OF PLACE, RECORDED AND NOT RESOLVED. This book says „Беху обоје из Александрије“ — both of them were from ALEXANDRIA — where doxologia’s long life calls her «a Christian virgin named Antonina, of the city called CRODAMNA», which is the name this folder is kept under. **The display name was not touched**: §10 reserves display names and a sourced correction to one is the author’s. Both readings are in the life. EVERYTHING ELSE CORROBORATES, DOWN TO THE SEVEN DAYS. The angel’s command, the soldier’s cloak thrown over her, the lowered head, the walk out through the guards, the exchange of places, the hands cut off, the beating on the bare body, the wounds burnt with candles, the pit of fire and the earth heaped over it, and the judge struck dumb at the hour of the martyrs’ death and tormented by an evil spirit **seven days** before it killed him — all of it is on these folders already, and this book names the judge «Фист» as doxologia names him Festus. **A third book agreeing to the seventh day is worth recording and changes nothing else.** `types` untouched on both and both corroborated: „Антонина чесна девица“ is her `virgin`, and „Александар царски војник“ is his `soldier`. `related` untouched, the two already pointing at each other and the entry naming nobody else but the judge, who has no folder and is the persecutor besides. No `locations`, the two cities disagreeing. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE FOLD IS DELIBERATE: `foldchk.py` returns `[('antonina-of-nicaea', 'sr')]`, so this makes a fold of two; the heading gives the bare forename and the city is in the body, which §6 does not let into a form.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Sfințit Mucenic Timotei, Episcopul Prusei, al Sfinților Mucenici Alexandru și Antonina, Glasul 4 (one troparion printed for the martyrs of the day together)

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their struggles received from thee, our God, the crowns of incorruption; for having thy strength they overthrew the tormentors and broke the powerless insolence of the demons. By their prayers save our souls, O Christ God.

hymns.text: Ξυνωρὶς ἡ ἁγία τῶν Μαρτύρων ὑμνείσθω μοί, σὺν τῷ εὐκλεεῖ Ἀλεξάνδρω, Ἀντωνίνα ἡ πάνσεμνος· ἀγάπη γὰρ καὶ πίστει εὐσεβεῖ, ἐκλάμψαντες ἐν ἄθλοις ἱεροίς, ἰαμάτων ἐφαπλούσι μαρμαρυγᾶς, τοὶς ποθῶ ἀνακράζουσα δόξα τῷ ἐνισχύσαντι ὑμᾶς, δόξα τῷ στεφανώσαντι, δόξα τῷ ἐνεργούντι δι' ὑμῶν, πάσιν ἰάματα

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος α’, Τῆς ἐρήμου πολίτης — the first of two apolytikia on the page of «Άγιοι Αλέξανδρος και Αντωνίνα», and the one that names them both; the second, «Οἱ Μάρτυρες σου Κύριε», is the common of martyrs

english.text: Let the holy pair of the martyrs be hymned by me — the all-modest Antonina together with the renowned Alexander; for shining out in sacred contests by love and by devout faith, they spread abroad the radiance of healings upon those who cry to them with longing: Glory to him who gave you strength, glory to him who crowned you, glory to him who through you works healings for all.

hymns.text: Τοὺς ἐν Χριστῷ, πνευματικοὺς ὁμαίμονας, καὶ ἐν ὁδοῖς, τῆς εὐσεβείας σύμφρονας, τὸν θεόφρονα Ἀλέξανδρον, σὺν Ἀντωνίνῃ μακαρίσωμεν· τοὺς ἄθλους γὰρ ἐκείνων καὶ τὰ στίγματα, ὡς μύρον εὐωδίας προσεδέξατο, ὁ τούτους δοξάσας ὡς ηὐδόκησε.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β’, Τοὺς ἀσφαλεῖς — the second of two kontakia on the page of «Άγιοι Αλέξανδρος και Αντωνίνα», and the one that names them both; the first, «Τῶν Μαρτύρων ἔλαμψεν», is a common

english.text: Let us call blessed the godly-minded Alexander together with Antonina, kinsfolk in the spirit in Christ and of one mind upon the ways of piety; for he who glorified them as he saw fit received their contests and their wounds as myrrh of sweet fragrance.

death.note: Two books on one flat year, and the folder held none. doxologia.ro's long life prints no year, and this folder's own life quotes saint.gr's head line «(; - 313)» without that year ever having reached `dates`. The Охридски пролог for 10. јун ст. ст. states it with a day: „преселише се у дворе Цара небескога 3. маја 313. године“. The 3 May is the date of the passing as this book gives it and not a day it keeps them on, which is the Julian 10 June; no feast was written on it (5 October 2026).
